The test image shows tomato leaves with dark bronze-mottled discoloration, irregular dark patches spread across the leaf surface, and a distinctive bronzing pattern. No white powder, no circular target-spot lesions, no water-soaked regions. This strongly suggests **Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV)**.

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference shows TSWV at a later wilting stage. The test image shows the earlier characteristic symptom: dark bronze mottling/discoloration across leaf surfaces, irregular dark patches, and the distinctive bronzed appearance — all hallmark early TSWV symptoms. The Bugwood ID 1575047 on the test image aligns with TSWV documentation patterns.

{"prediction": "Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus", "confidence": 0.82, "reasoning": "The test image shows tomato leaves with dark bronze mottling, irregular dark patches spread diffusely across the leaf surface, and a characteristic bronzed discoloration pattern. This is the hallmark early-stage symptom of Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (TSWV). No target-spot rings (ruling out Early Blight), no white powder (ruling out Powdery Mildew), no water-soaked lesions (ruling out Late Blight or Phytophthora). The diffuse dark bronzing across the entire leaf is most consistent with TSWV."}
